Custom PDE studio

Define evolution equations, run simulations and compare numerical resolutions.

1D + 2D · Periodic & bounded domains

Experiment settings

01

Set each field and edge below. Dirichlet fixes the field value. Neumann prescribes ∂n u: −u_x at left, +u_x at right, −u_y at bottom, +u_y at top. Zero Neumann means no diffusive flux. Robin sets αu + β∂n u = g, with constant α, β ≥ 0 and α + β > 0. The target g may depend on x, y, t and parameters. For convection, use α = Bi, β = 1, g = Bi*ambient.

1D fourth-order evolution: prescribe two independent linear boundary rows at each endpoint. The leading term must be −kappa*Dx(u,4), kappa > 0. Second/third derivative coefficients may have either sign. Start with a fourth-order preset.

Named constants separated by semicolons. Use * for multiplication and ^ for powers.

    Export results

    Exports always describe the last successful run, including its equation and method.

    Python reference

    JSON includes every field and saved frame. Import reruns the model; share links contain the model configuration.

    Recompute with an independent Python integrator

    Install NumPy and SciPy, then run python studio_reference.py phaseatlas-custom-experiment.json. This uses NumPy FFT for periodic domains or independent finite-volume or finite-difference stencils for bounded domains, with SciPy DOP853 or BDF instead of the browser time integrator. Use N ≤ 128 in 1D or N ≤ 32 per axis in 2D; the checker selects BDF automatically for fourth-order bounded problems, or add --method BDF for another stiff small-grid check.

    Equation syntax and supported models

    Expression syntax

    Fields & coordinates
    u, v, w, x, y, t, Lx, Ly, pi, e. Only active fields and coordinates are available.
    Spatial derivatives
    Dx(u,1), Dx(u,4), Dy(v,2), lap(u), biharm(u). In periodic mode, derivatives may act on expressions: lap(u^3). Second-order bounded mode requires derivatives directly on fields. Fourth-order 1D mode also accepts first derivatives of flux expressions, such as Dx(u^3,1).
    Arithmetic & functions
    + - * / ^, sin cos tanh exp log sqrt abs min max. Initial data use coordinates and parameters; references also accept t.

    What this solver supports

    One to three real fields on a 1D interval or 2D rectangle. Write equations as first-order evolution systems. Periodic mode supports spatial derivatives up to total order four. Second-order bounded mode supports constant, non-negative, diagonal diffusion with reactions and forcing, plus first derivatives when the differentiated field has positive diffusion in that direction.

    Periodic mode uses Fourier ETDRK4. Dirichlet/Neumann/passive Robin mode uses cell-centered finite volumes and SBDF2 with implicit diffusion. Boundary data can vary with time and along each edge. Reactions and transport are explicit; inspect time-step and grid refinement.

    Fourth-order bounded mode supports 1D systems with a negative constant diagonal fourth-derivative coefficient. Each endpoint has two custom linear conditions using u and its first three normal derivatives. All constant same-field linear terms are implicit. Coupled reactions and first derivatives remain explicit. Two-dimensional fourth-order problems and standalone third-order equations are not supported. Pure transport needs inflow/outflow handling. Elliptic boundary-value problems, cross/variable diffusion on bounded domains, arbitrary geometries, shocks without regularization and constrained systems need other methods. Reference formulas are used for field comparisons and sampled residual checks.

    Theory: Kassam & Trefethen, fourth-order time stepping. The front laboratory retains its separate, model-specific analytic checks.
